notes: Paths are relative to the repository root, not to this file.
WHY 4x3 AND NOT THE PRODUCT'S OLD 3:2. flag-icons publishes two sets, 4x3
and 1x1, and normalises every flag into whichever box is asked for. A
third ratio would mean letterboxing the pack's own artwork inside a box
the pack did not draw, so the Compose side follows the corpus rather than
the corpus following a number that was chosen before the corpus was.
WHY 192x144 AND ONE SIZE. The widest a flag is drawn is 36 dp, in the two
country pickers; the chip draws 24 dp. Thirty-six dp on the densest
shipping bucket, xxxhdpi at 4x, is 144 pixels, so 192 is a third more than
the product can currently ask for and every use downscales. One size
rather than a bucket per density because the pack is fetched once for the
whole device and a density-qualified pack would be several packs, each
needing its own row, its own digest and its own publication decision.
WHY THE RASTERISER IS PINNED. A rasteriser's output is part of the
artifact's bytes. A different librsvg antialiases an edge differently and
the digest moves with no input having changed, which would make a catalog
row that was true yesterday false today. The pair is refused on mismatch
for the same reason the launcher-icon tool refuses an unpinned cwebp.
WHY THE PATH CARRIES NO PLUS SIGN. The browser's own second check,
IsRelativePath in taffy-core/browser/core_asset_validation.cc, permits
only a-z, 0-9, '.', '-', '_' and the separator -- a strict subset of what
the catalog generator's PATH_SEGMENT regex accepts. A revision spelled
with a '+' would generate cleanly and be refused on the device, so the
revision here is spelled with a hyphen and the path embeds it verbatim.
WHY THE LICENCE TRAVELS INSIDE THE ZIP. The pack reaches a device through
the delivery plane and is in no build graph, so nothing carries the MIT
notice onto the generated credits page for it. A LICENSE member is the
only copy that arrives with the bytes it covers.
